# Error codes

<!-- Generated by scripts/Update-AutomatedPackagingErrorCodes.ps1 from docs/reference/error-codes.md
     of the product repository, commit a41e3b1. Do not edit this page by hand. -->

This page lists every `AP-` error code of AppVentiX Automated Packaging, with its cause and what to do. The product generates this list from its own code. [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#common-error-codes) has the short list of common codes.

A code never gets a different meaning. A code that is no longer used stays in the list, marked retired.

*Copied from the product's error-code register of 2026-11-05 (commit a41e3b1).*

## `AP-HV` — VM lifecycle

### `AP-HV-006` — The worker stopped unexpectedly

During a job, the worker stopped, stopped responding, or restarted, and the host did not ask for this. The System log of the worker records a restart after a stop error or a reset. This is a failure of Windows in the worker. An installer that restarts the worker is AP-IN-009.

**What to do:**

- Read the failure detail of the job. It tells if the worker stopped, stopped responding, or restarted after an error. If the worker stopped, read the Hyper-V-Worker event log on the host for the reason. The job reverts the worker, so the logs in the worker are gone.
- Make sure that the host has enough free memory to keep an 8 GB worker running.
- Click Put it back for the worker on the Images screen. Then run the job again.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-HV-007` — The worker is already running a job

Another job has a lease on the worker that this job needs, so this job did not touch the worker. A worker runs one job at a time. Other workers can run other jobs at the same time.

**What to do:**

- Wait until the other job is done, or cancel it on the Jobs screen.
- Let the planner select the worker. It uses another free worker for the same target.
- If no job is running, a stopped process still has the lease. Open the application: the Jobs screen offers to recover the job.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-HV-008` — The worker could not be created

The product did not create the worker, and it built nothing. A virtual machine with that name exists, its disk exists, or the host has no space for it. Nothing changed, so a machine that holds work stays as it is.

**What to do:**

- Select a different worker name. If a failed build left a worker with that name, remove it under Incomplete machines on the Images screen. The product removes only its own workers.
- Check the free space where the workers are kept. One worker needs at least 60 GB. Use 200 GB for several workers.
- Make sure that the name starts with the managed prefix. The product acts only on names with that prefix.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-HV-009` — The virtual TPM could not be turned on

Windows 11 Setup needs TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. The product could not create the key protector that a virtual TPM needs. The product stops here, because Setup would refuse the worker later and not give a clear reason.

**What to do:**

- On a managed host, check if the Host Guardian Service configuration blocks Set-VMKeyProtector.
- Make sure that the host supports virtualisation-based security and that the worker is Generation 2.
- Build the worker on a host that can give it a virtual TPM.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-HV-010` — The worker could not be removed

The product did not remove the worker, and it deleted nothing. The worker is running, it does not exist, or Hyper-V did not remove it. This refusal is the safe result, because a removal cannot be undone.

**What to do:**

- Stop the worker first. A running worker is in use, and a removal never turns off its power.
- Check if the worker is already removed. The product reports a second removal of a worker as a failure, not as a success.
- Make sure that the name starts with the managed prefix. The product acts only on names with that prefix.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-HV-011` — The worker could not be put back to its baseline

The product could not apply the baseline checkpoint, so the worker stays as the last action left it. No job gets this worker until an operator acts. A worker in an unknown state can put the files of one job into the package of the next job.

**What to do:**

- Make sure that the baseline checkpoint is still on the worker. An Update seals the checkpoint again, and a seal that stops halfway can leave no checkpoint.
- Check the free space where the workers are kept. Hyper-V writes the checkpoint before it removes the old state.
- Make sure that no dialog for this worker waits in Hyper-V Manager.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-HV-012` — AI agents do not remove workers on this host

An AI agent asked through MCP to remove a worker or to forget an image. On this host, agents do not do this. Removing a worker deletes the machine and its disks.

**What to do:**

- Remove the worker or forget the image on the Images screen, or with the command line.
- To let agents do it, go to Settings > AI agents (MCP). Tick "Agents can remove workers and forget images", then click Save.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-NW` — Channel and network

### `AP-NW-004` — The worker's clock could not be corrected

The host set the worker's clock and measured it again, and the difference is still too large. If the difference stays equal to the age of the checkpoint, Time Synchronization is off on the worker.

**Observed:** The difference stayed equal to the age of the checkpoint after each correction.

**What to do:**

- Turn on the Time Synchronization integration service on the worker.
- Make sure that the clock of the host is correct.
- Update the image when the worker's clock is correct. The Update seals a new baseline checkpoint.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-NW-005` — The connection to the agent was lost

The worker and the agent are still running, but the connection to the host dropped and did not come back. This is a fault of the connection, not of the worker.

**What to do:**

- Check if the network mode changed during the job. A change closes the connection.
- Make sure that the port ACLs of the virtual switch still let the agent reach the host on its listener port.
- Look for a rule in the host firewall that blocks the listener.

**Retry:** Yes. This is a transient condition.

### `AP-NW-006` — The DNS sinkhole is not working

During the self test at startup, a name took more than one second to resolve, or did not resolve. If nobody sees this now, a conversion stops for 12 seconds later, with no clear reason.

**Observed:** A host had nine inbound Allow rules for UDP, and none of them applied to the responder. So the host dropped the worker's query before the sinkhole saw it.

**What to do:**

- Run host preparation. It creates the inbound firewall rule that the responder needs.
- Look for inbound Block rules named 'Query User' for Windows PowerShell. Windows creates them again, and they stop the sinkhole with no error.
- Make sure that the responder listens on the host's address on the internal switch, not only on a wildcard address.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-NW-007` — The worker sent more than this host accepts

The host refused an upload that was larger than its limit, for one file or for the whole job. The host does not trust the size that the agent declares. After an installer runs in a worker, the worker is not trusted. So the host applies its own limit while the data arrives.

**What to do:**

- Check if the package is really this large. A capture that includes a full user profile can be.
- If it is, increase MaxJobUploadMegabytes in agent-channel.json. One file can be half of this value at most.
- If the size is not what you expect, check the exclusion set of the image before you increase the limit.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-AG` — Agent and bootstrapper

### `AP-AG-002` — The image's bootstrapper is too old for this agent

The bootstrapper in the image declares a contract version that the agent does not accept. The bootstrapper changes rarely, so this is rare. When it occurs, the image needs a new build.

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the image from media on the Images screen. The new build has the current bootstrapper.
- Until then, use an image whose bootstrapper agrees with the agent.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AG-003` — The agent is not signed correctly

The Authenticode check of the agent failed. A worker makes signed packages for customers, so it never runs an unsigned or changed agent.

**What to do:**

- Repair or install the product again. This puts back a correct agent.
- If the problem continues, somebody can have changed the installation on disk. Check the installation folder.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AG-005` — The agent stopped running inside the worker

The worker is still running, but the agent process stopped. The worker is healthy, and the agent is not.

**What to do:**

- Collect the agent log from the worker before the job reverts it. The revert removes the log.
- Look in the Application event log of the worker for a crash record.
- Run the job again. If it fails at the same stage again, click Collect support information under Settings > Diagnostics, and send the file to AppVentiX support.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-AG-006` — The agent in the image could not be updated

The host offered the image a newer agent, and the update did not complete. The worker still runs the old agent. An old agent causes failures that look like faults in a different part, so the product reports it.

**What to do:**

- Make sure that the worker can reach the host on the listener port. The agent gets its new version through the same connection.
- Make sure that the new agent is signed and that the image trusts its certificate.
- If the update continues to fail, click Update for the worker on the Images screen. Step 6 installs the current agent.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-AG-007` — This worker's image does not record an agent identity

Each worker gets its own client certificate during preparation, and the image records its thumbprint. A job token is bound to that thumbprint, so a worker without a thumbprint cannot get a token. Usually, the image was built before the product recorded thumbprints.

**What to do:**

- Click Update for this worker on the Images screen. Step 6 enrols the worker again and records the thumbprint.
- If the Update cannot run, rebuild the image from media.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AG-008` — The worker refused the password of its packaging account

The host signs in to the worker with the password that it kept when it built the worker. The worker refused this password. Then Windows also refuses its automatic sign-in, so the agent does not start. Usually, the worker was built before 0.2.14: its password expires 42 days after the build.

**Observed:** The worker's own log refuses the automatic sign-in with 0xC0000071 (password expired). PowerShell Direct answers "The credential is invalid".

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the worker from media on the Images screen. A worker built with 0.2.14 or later keeps its password.
- If the worker was built with 0.2.14 or later, its stored password and the worker do not agree. Rebuild the worker.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-IM` — Worker image

### `AP-IM-008` — The image's exclusion set is incomplete

The exclusion set does not repeat the entries that the packaging tool excludes by default. The tool replaces its own list with the list that it gets, so it captures each entry that is not repeated.

**Observed:** The packaging tool's own logs and MsixGenerator.ConversionState.xml were in the package. They made the package about two times larger.

**What to do:**

- Click Update for the worker on the Images screen. Step 10 measures the exclusion set again, with the default entries.
- Compare the set with the shipped baseline. A set that is smaller than the default entries is always wrong.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-009` — The packaging tool's licence is not registered in the image

The packaging tool is installed, but its offline licence is not registered for the account that runs conversions. The installation is not sufficient: the licence needs a second registration call.

**Observed:** The packaging tool was gone after a restart, or conversions failed with 0x80072EE7 or 'the file cannot be accessed by the system'.

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the image from media on the Images screen. Step 5 installs the packaging tool and registers its licence with the -Register call.
- Make sure that the registration ran as the account that the agent uses.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-010` — The packaging driver is missing from the image

The filter driver of the packaging tool is not installed, or its build does not agree with the Windows release of the worker. A capture cannot run without it.

**Observed:** 0x8024402C when the driver was downloaded, or 0x800f081f CBS_E_SOURCE_MISSING.

**What to do:**

- Stage the Features on Demand media for the Windows release of the worker. Then rebuild the image from media.
- The staging-media guide tells which Features on Demand file each Windows release needs.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-011` — Image preparation ran in the wrong order

Hardening turned off Windows Update before the packaging driver was installed. The driver must come first, because its installation needs Windows Update.

**Observed:** Add-WindowsCapability failed with 0x80240438, because Windows Update was turned off.

**What to do:**

- Rebuild the image from media. The build installs the packaging driver at step 5, before the hardening at step 8.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-012` — The worker does not have enough free disk space

A capture needs space for the installed application, the working files of the packaging tool and the package, all at the same time. The minimum is a setting in Advanced, and its default is 10 GB.

**What to do:**

- If this application is small, set a lower Minimum free disk space (GB) in Advanced.
- Give the worker a larger disk. Or click Put it back on the Images screen to revert the worker to its baseline.
- The space that a capture needs does not follow the size of the installer. In one conversion, a 283 MB installer became 2.7 GB of files.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-013` — The installation media is missing or does not agree with the worker

A file that the build needs is not at its configured location. Or the Features on Demand media is for a different Windows release than the worker. Media for a different release does not give the capture driver. The product ships no Microsoft files, so you supply all media.

**What to do:**

- Check the configured media paths.
- Use Features on Demand media for the Windows release of the worker. 22621 media is for Windows 11 22H2, and 26100 media is for 24H2 and later.
- Make sure that the packaging tool package and its licence are both present. The licence is a separate file, and it is the file that operators most often forget.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-014` — Windows did not finish installing

The unattended installation did not get to a signed-in desktop in the time allowed. If Setup rejects the answer file, it waits at a prompt that nobody sees. Until the time ends, this looks like a slow installation.

**What to do:**

- Open the console of the worker and read what Setup waits for.
- Make sure that the answer file is attached as a DVD drive. Also make sure that the installation media has the edition that the answer file names.
- Check the free space on the host. An installation that fills the volume stops with no error.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IM-015` — Tamper Protection is on, so the hardening would not stay

Nothing in a running Windows can turn off Tamper Protection, not even SYSTEM. A protected process enforces it below the ACL layer. Settings that change while it is on change back after a few seconds, with no error. Then Defender activity is in each capture, with no visible cause.

**What to do:**

- Turn off Tamper Protection in Windows Security, then run this again. PowerShell, WMI and the registry cannot turn it off.
- Better: shut down the worker and run scripts\image\Disable-WorkerDefender.ps1 -WorkerName <name>. It turns off the six Defender services in the offline SYSTEM hive, so Defender never starts. This works on every build. On the build that the product installs, Windows reverts what the answer file writes during specialize.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-016` — The runtimes could not be installed in an isolated worker

The runtimes that the packaging tool needs are not staged on the host. An isolated worker has no route to a package source. The product does not open the network of an isolated worker to get them.

**What to do:**

- Stage the runtimes on the host for the image preparation.
- The runtimes are the Visual C++ runtimes, the .NET Desktop Runtime and the WebView2 runtime.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-017` — Calibration did not make a usable exclusion set

Too few null captures completed, or together they found nothing. Captures of one image differ more than Windows builds do. So one empty result tells nothing, and the product does not use it. Four captures from one checkpoint found 534, 0, 534 and 534 registry keys.

**What to do:**

- Run at least four null captures, one of them about three minutes long. Use all the entries that they found together.
- First restart the worker and let it settle. A calibration straight after a hardening change measures the effects of that change, not the normal state of the image.
- Make sure that the capture driver is installed and that the packaging tool starts. A capture that did not run gives an empty result, which looks like a quiet image.

**Retry:** Yes. This is a transient condition.

### `AP-IM-018` — The image's calibration has expired

The exclusion set is 180 days old or more. Since it was measured, Windows can have changed what an idle worker writes. The job does not fail. Instead, the package can contain changes that are not from the application. The product still runs jobs on the image, and marks it Update recommended.

**What to do:**

- Click Update for the worker on the Images screen. Step 10 measures the exclusion set again, and step 11 seals a new baseline checkpoint.
- If nobody maintains the image now, forget it, so that no job can select it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-019` — A script the product ships is not signed like the product

A signed product runs only scripts that are signed like the product. This script is unsigned, changed after signing, or signed by somebody else. These scripts run elevated on this host or in a worker. So the step stopped before it ran or copied the script. An unsigned product does not do this check.

**What to do:**

- Repair or install the product again. The installer puts back the scripts that it signed.
- If somebody changed a script on purpose, sign it again with the product's certificate. The product never runs a changed script.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-020` — A preparation step stopped on an error it has no code for

A step that builds or updates a worker ran a Windows or Hyper-V operation. The operation failed with an error that the product does not know. The message is the error of the operation, and it names the step.

**What to do:**

- Read the preparation log, prep-<worker>-<run>.log, in the Logs folder of the working directory. Its last lines name the step and give the full error.
- The step leaves the worker as it was. A new worker that did not get to step 12 is under Incomplete machines. A worker in an Update stays on the Images screen. When the cause is fixed, click Put it back or Rebuild from media.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IM-021` — Windows could not be activated against the KMS server

At step 9, the host opened its KMS relay, set Windows in the worker to use it, and asked for activation. Windows refused, or could not reach the server. The message names the server and the code from Windows. The worker stays on the internal switch. Only the host talks to the KMS server, for three minutes at most.

**What to do:**

- Check the KMS server in the message from this host. The host resolves the name and makes the connection. A name that only the network of the workers knows does not resolve here.
- 0xC004F074 means that no KMS server answered. Check the name, the port and the firewalls between this host and the server. Also check the inbound rule for TCP 1688: Prepare this host under Settings > This host creates it.
- 0xC004F038 means that the server answered, but it does not count enough clients yet. 0xC004F042 means that it does not activate this edition. The KMS administrator must fix both.
- When the server is correct, build the image again or update it. An Update can change the KMS server.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IM-022` — A prerequisite could not be installed on the image

Step 7 installs the prerequisites of the image in order, before hardening. One of them failed. It returned a code that is not a success code, or asked for a restart that is not allowed. Or its detection rule did not find it after the installation, or it did not finish in time. The message names the item, its ID and its answer.

**What to do:**

- Open the item on the Prerequisites screen. Check its arguments, success codes and detection rule. An installer without its silent switch waits for a click that nobody can give.
- If an item needs a restart, tick Restart allowed. The codes 3010 and 1641 ask for a restart.
- Items must install offline. A worker has no route out, so a web installer or a bootstrapper that downloads files fails.
- When the item is correct, build or update the image again. The step leaves the worker as it was.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IM-023` — The image must be updated before it can run a job

The product compares each image with this version of the product and with the settings of this host. This image is too old for one of them, or a setting changed after the build. A job on it would fail. So the product did not start the job. The message names each reason.

**What to do:**

- Open the Images screen. A red mark shows the image, and its details list each reason and the remedy.
- Click Update for the worker. Step 6 installs the current agent, and step 12 writes the current settings.
- If the reason says Rebuild from media, click Rebuild from media for the worker.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-IN` — Installer and capture

### `AP-IN-007` — Restart limit exceeded (retired)

**RETIRED. Never raised.** The plan withdrew restart support, so this limit cannot occur. The code stays recorded, because a code is never used again.

### `AP-IN-008` — The job ran out of time

The whole job took longer than its limit. AP-IN-010 is different: one run of the packaging tool took too long. The two codes point to different problems.

**What to do:**

- Find the stage that was running when the time ended. A large installer can need a longer limit.
- If the job did nothing for a long time, look for an installer that waits for an answer in a dialog.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IN-009` — The worker restarted during the capture

Something restarted the worker during the capture. The packaging tool cannot continue a capture after a restart: it continues and then crashes, or it cannot continue (measured). The product handles an installer that only asks for a restart, with exit code 3010 or 1641. Here, the installer or a program that it started restarted Windows itself.

**Observed:** NullReferenceException in TranslateShortcutsToApplicationNode, an empty output folder, and HKLM\Software\Microsoft\MSIXPackagingTool\Resume still present.

**What to do:**

- Look for a vendor switch that stops the restart, for example /norestart, REBOOT=ReallySuppress for an MSI, or a documented no-restart option. Then the work for the restart runs inside the capture.
- If the installer always restarts Windows, the product cannot capture it. Package the application from a reference machine on which it is already installed.
- Do not only try again. The same thing occurs each time.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-010` — The packaging tool stopped responding

One run of the packaging tool took longer than its time limit, so the product stopped the tool and its processes. The tool can stop on an internal error and wait for a key that nobody presses. So the product cannot rely on the tool to exit.

**Observed:** The tool printed 'Press any key to close this window...'. The process stayed at almost zero CPU and was still running ten minutes later. One conversion waited 50 minutes with a 40-minute timeout.

**What to do:**

- Look in the log of the packaging tool for 'Press any key to close this window'. This is the case of a wait for a key.
- If the log ends with 'Installer still running', the installer or a program that it started did not exit. The packaging tool waits for all of them. Usually, the installer starts its application when it finishes. Turn that off in its arguments, for VS Code with /MERGETASKS=!runcode.
- If the installer ran at almost zero CPU with no output, its silent arguments are probably wrong. It then shows a window on a desktop that nobody sees. Check the silent switches first.
- Try again only when you know which case it was.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-IN-011` — This installer needs silent-install arguments

An .exe installer has no arguments. The packaging tool refuses such a template, but only after a worker has started. So the product stops the job when it makes the template.

**Observed:** The packaging tool refused to read the template and exited with 1, after a worker had started.

**What to do:**

- Give the silent switches of the installer. Look first in the vendor's documentation, but it is not always correct. One documented --silent switch still showed a window, and /quiet /norestart worked.
- Look for an MSI inside the installer, or an MSI version of it. An MSI has a standard silent mode.
- If it has no silent mode, the product cannot package it today. Interactive installs are not available yet.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-012` — The installer did not report success

The installer ran and exited with a code that is not in the list of valid codes of this job. Usually, the silent arguments are wrong. The installer started, could not do what the arguments said, and stopped.

**Observed:** The packaging tool reported an installer exit code that was not zero. The capture completed and made a package with almost nothing in it.

**What to do:**

- Compare the silent switches with the vendor's documentation, and then test them. The documented --silent switch of one application still showed a window that nobody saw. /quiet /norestart worked.
- 1603 is the general MSI failure. Usually, a prerequisite is missing or the arguments are not correct. 1618 means that another installation is running.
- If the code is correct for this installer, add it to Valid installer exit codes in Advanced. You cannot add 3010 and 1641, and you do not need them. They ask for a restart, and the install wrapper runs that work inside the capture.
- Check if the installer installed anything. An empty capture with an exit code that is not zero means that the installer did nothing.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-013` — The installer left work that only a restart can do

The installer finished, and left work that Windows does only during a restart. This is files to replace or delete at the next boot, or RunOnceEx work. The capture cannot do that work, so the package would contain the files as they were before the restart. The message and the installation log name each entry. A file deleted at the restart in a folder that the package leaves out does not cause this. An example is the temporary folder. The job shows a note instead.

**What to do:**

- Usually, a file replaced at the restart was in use during the installation. On a clean worker this is rare. Look for a service or process that the installer starts and then updates. Also look for a vendor switch that prevents this.
- Look for a version of the installer that completes without a restart. For example, a newer version, an MSI instead of a bundle, or an option that installs everything in one pass.
- Do not only try again. The same thing occurs each time.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-014` — A prerequisite could not be installed before the capture

The job installs its prerequisites on the reverted worker in order, before it captures the application. One of them failed. It returned a code that is not a success code, or asked for a restart that is not allowed. Or its detection rule did not find it after the installation, or it did not finish in time. Nothing was captured. The message names the item, its ID and its answer.

**What to do:**

- Open the item on the Prerequisites screen. Check its arguments, success codes and detection rule. An installer without its silent switch waits for a click that nobody can give.
- If an item needs a restart, tick Restart allowed. The codes 3010 and 1641 ask for a restart.
- Items must install offline. A web installer or a bootstrapper that downloads files fails on a worker.
- A PowerShell 7 script item needs the PowerShell 7 item. If the image does not have PowerShell 7, the job installs it first.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-015` — The files beside the installer could not be staged

The job had to send the files and folders beside the installer, or the transforms of an MSI, to the worker. It could not. After the job was planned, the folder became a drive root, got a link, or became larger than the limit. Or a file changed size or led to a different place while the job sent it. Or a transform was gone or was a link, or the worker could not unpack the files. Nothing was captured.

**What to do:**

- Keep the installer in its own folder, with only the files that it needs. Do not change that folder while the job runs.
- The limit is 4 GB and 20,000 files beside the installer. The product refuses links (junctions, symbolic links) and files with a second name (hard links). They can point anywhere on the host, so replace them with copies.
- Make sure that each transform is still at the location that you selected, as a file and not as a link.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-IN-016` — The installer changed after the job was planned, so it did not run

The job recorded the SHA-256 of the installer when the job was planned. When the job sent the installer to the worker, the file was different or gone. Or it was a link, had a second name, or led to a different folder. The worker did not run it, and nothing was captured.

**What to do:**

- Do not change the installer or its folder while the job runs. Then build the job again.
- Keep installers where only the people who package can change them. A share that other people can write to is a risk.
- The product refuses links (junctions, symbolic links) and files with a second name (hard links). Replace them with a copy.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-AN` — Pre-analysis

### `AP-AN-010` — This MSI schedules a restart

The analysis found a ScheduleReboot or ForceReboot action in the action table of the installer. This is a note, not a refusal. The MSI runs with /norestart, and the install wrapper runs its RunOnce work inside the capture. If the MSI schedules files to replace at the restart, the product refuses the package after the capture (AP-IN-013).

**Observed:** A ScheduleReboot or ForceReboot action in the action table of the MSI.

**What to do:**

- You do not need to do anything before the build. If the job ends with AP-IN-013, look for a vendor switch or transform that prevents the restart.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-AN-011` — This installer declares a Windows service

The MSI declares services in its ServiceInstall table. The capture includes them and they work. But the package then has the restricted capabilities packagedServices and localSystemServices. This is information, not a refusal.

**Observed:** An MSI service was packaged and deployed, ran from inside the package, and was removed correctly at uninstall.

**What to do:**

- You do not need to do anything. The package needs restricted capabilities, which has an effect on Store submission and on some deployment policies.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-AN-012` — This file could not be read as an installer

The Build screen reads the application name, publisher and version from the installer. This file is not the type that its extension shows, or the product cannot read its data. You can still type the job details. The product does not guess from a file that does not open.

**What to do:**

- Make sure that the download is complete. A truncated MSI has the correct extension, but its database cannot be read.
- If the file is an EXE that contains an installer, there is no data to read. Type the name, publisher and version, and give the silent switches.
- If other tools open this MSI correctly, keep the file. Contact support with this code: the database opens in other tools but not here.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-AN-013` — This installer installs a driver

The analysis found a device or kernel driver in the MSI, so the product refused the job before a worker started. An MSIX package cannot install a driver. The capture would leave the driver out, or keep a driver file that Windows never loads.

**What to do:**

- Deploy the driver separately, with the vendor's installer, Intune or Configuration Manager. Then package the application without it, if the vendor offers an installation without the driver.
- If the driver is for optional hardware, look for a vendor property that skips the driver feature. Add it to the silent arguments.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-PK` — Packaging

### `AP-PK-004` — The package contains parts of this product

The scan after the capture found the installation folder of the agent, or the product marker, in the files or the registry of the package. The product does not deliver this to customers, so the job fails.

**What to do:**

- Make sure that the fixed exclusions of the image include the installation folder of the agent.
- Make sure that a null capture on this image is empty. If a null capture contains these files, the problem is in the image, not in the application.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-005` — The package has no application to start

The manifest has no Applications element, or it is empty. The package installs and does nothing. The installer created no Start menu shortcut, so the packaging tool had no entry point to make.

**Observed:** Exit code 0, a package that installs correctly, and nothing to start. The packaging tool logged only 'A shortcut with target ... was not detected'.

**What to do:**

- Check if the installer creates a shortcut. Many tools that install for the whole machine do not.
- If the application really has no shortcut, add one in the installer. Or give the entry point before packaging.
- The packaging tool logs this only as information about a shortcut that it did not detect. So you do not find it as an error in its output.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-006` — The package declares a framework it does not use

The packaging tool writes a Windows App SDK dependency into the manifest of each package that has an entry point. It does this whatever the package contains. If the dependency stays, the package does not deploy.

**Observed:** Add-AppxPackage failed with 0x80073CF3, 'depends on a framework that could not be found'. It named Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.1.4 for a plain runFullTrust package. The packaging tool writes the same fixed version into each package, measured on six.

**What to do:**

- The product removes this dependency itself. This code means that the scan of the package files could not decide.
- If the application really is a Windows App SDK application, make sure that the target machines have the correct runtime version.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-007` — Something that should have been excluded is in the package

The check after the conversion found a path that the exclusion set should have removed. An exclusion with an incorrect path form excludes nothing, and the packaging tool reports nothing. So the product checks the result.

**Observed:** Three excluded entries were in a package, one of them a 7.8 MB copy of the source MSI.

**What to do:**

- Compare the path form of the exclusion with the documented syntax rules.
- An entry reported as UNVERIFIABLE has no mapping. This is not a pass: a person must examine it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-008` — Some services were not carried into the package

The capture contains services, but the manifest has no windows.service extension for them. The installer created these services while it ran, and did not declare them. The packaging tool drops them with no warning. The product reports this and does not refuse the package. Usually, the service is an auto-updater that nobody wants in a package.

**Observed:** The installer created services while it ran. They were in the capture but not in the manifest, and the packaging tool gave no warning.

**What to do:**

- Check the service names in the report. Usually, you can safely lose an updater service, and often you want to.
- If the application needs one of them, it does not work from the package. It needs a different packaging method.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-PK-009` — The package contains a RunOnce entry that will never run

The installer registered work to do after a restart. Windows reads RunOnce from the real registry, never from the virtual registry of a package. So that work never occurs, and the package looks correct.

**Observed:** HKLM\...\CurrentVersion\RunOnce was in the virtual registry of a package after a conversion that was otherwise successful.

**What to do:**

- Check what the entry does. Usually, you can safely lose a file cleanup or a one-time migration. You cannot lose the last part of the installation.
- If the application needs that work, the installer must complete its work after the restart before the capture. If it cannot, the product cannot package it this way.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-PK-010` — The package was built, but its export did not complete

The job succeeded and the package is in the output folder. But the copy to the export location on Settings did not complete. The warning names the step that failed. If the package was not copied, the tools that read that location do not see this build. If only the self-signed certificate or the dependency list was not written, the package is there without it.

**What to do:**

- Make sure that this host can reach the export location on Settings, and that the computer's account can write there. The host service writes each export as the computer's account. Check location on Settings tests exactly this.
- On a share (\\server\share), "access denied" usually comes from the permissions of the share, not of the folder. Their default is Everyone: Read, which refuses each write through the share path. Give the computer's account Change on the share. For a share on this host, you can also use the folder's local path.
- The product refuses a package folder or a Certificates folder under the export location that is a junction or a symbolic link. It does not write through the link. Remove the link, and the export creates the folder itself.
- Copy the package from the output folder yourself, or build the job again when the location works.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-PK-011` — The Package Support Framework could not be applied

The job turns on the Package Support Framework, but its files on this host cannot be used. They are missing, changed since they were downloaded, or not signed by TMurgent Technologies LLP. TMurgent publishes the release that the product uses. The message names the files. Nothing was put into the package.

**What to do:**

- On Settings > This host, on the Package Support Framework card, click Get PSF (or Get … again). It downloads the pinned release from GitHub and checks each file before it keeps it.
- On a host without internet, copy the files of that release into the PSF folder that the card names.
- If the job does not need PSF, turn it off in the Advanced settings of the job.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-PK-012` — A prerequisite cannot be used

An image or a job needs a prerequisite that cannot be used. Its files in the Distro\Prerequisites folder of the working directory are missing, or do not agree with the hash recorded when they were stored. Or the item was removed from the library, is not in it, or depends on an item that was. Nothing was installed.

**What to do:**

- Open the Prerequisites screen. It shows each item whose files do not agree. Replace the files there, which records the new hash.
- You cannot use a removed item again. Leave it out of the image or job. Or add it again on the Prerequisites screen, where it gets a new ID.
- Only the Prerequisites screen must write into Distro\Prerequisites.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-SG` — Signing

### `AP-SG-005` — The publisher change cannot be bridged

To bridge a publisher change, the catalog must be signed with the previous certificate. Its private key is not available, so the new package cannot continue the identity of deployed packages.

**What to do:**

- If the old private key exists, import it and run the job again.
- If not, the new package has a different identity. Deployed installations do not upgrade in place: remove them, then install the new package.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-006` — Adding the certificate trust did not return

A write to a certificate store opened a consent dialog in a session with no interactive desktop. Nobody could answer it, so the call did not return.

**Observed:** An addition to CurrentUser\Root opened a consent dialog in a session with no desktop. The call waited until something stopped it.

**What to do:**

- Use LocalMachine\Root from an elevated process, not CurrentUser\Root, which shows a prompt.
- This trust setup is only for development. A certificate from a CA needs none of it.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-007` — The package's Publisher does not match the signing certificate

MSIX requires that the Publisher in the manifest is exactly the same as the subject of the signing certificate. Signing stops at any difference, also a difference in spaces or in the order of attributes.

**Observed:** signtool refused the package with 0x8007000B, 'the app manifest publisher name must match the subject name of the signing certificate'.

**What to do:**

- The product copies the certificate subject to the Publisher before it signs. If you see this code, that step did not run, or the certificate changed after it.
- Compare the two exactly. 'CN=Contoso, O=Contoso' and 'CN=Contoso,O=Contoso' are different, and only one of them works.
- If the publisher really changed, Windows sees the new package as a different identity. Existing installations do not upgrade in place. See AP-SG-005 about bridging.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-008` — The package could not be signed

SignTool refused the signature or could not complete it, and the manifest publisher was not the cause. The package is not signed, and it has not left this machine.

**What to do:**

- For Azure Artifact Signing, check the service principal of the profile on Settings > Signing. It must have the Artifact Signing Certificate Profile Signer role on the profile.
- For a certificate in the Windows store, make sure that it is still in LocalMachine\My and still has its private key. It must not be on a hardware token that waits for a PIN.
- If the timestamp server was not available, the file stays fully unsigned, not partly signed. So you can safely try again when the network works.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-SG-009` — The publisher has changed too many times to bridge

Each change of signing publisher adds one bridging artifact to the package, and Windows applies five at most. This change needs a sixth. So the package cannot keep the identity of the installations that are already deployed.

**What to do:**

- Sign with a publisher that is already in the chain. This needs no new artifact.
- If not, the new package has a different identity. Deployed installations do not upgrade in place: remove them, then install the new package.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-010` — The tools that sign packages can be changed by somebody who is not an administrator

The application runs signtool, makecat and makeappx elevated from the Tools folder. They work on the package in its job folder, and the application signs the packages in the Packages folder. An account that is not an administrator can change one of these folders, or a folder above them. So the tool did not start, and the job, Retry signing or the signing test stopped.

**What to do:**

- Run host preparation (AutomatedPackaging.PrepareHost.exe) and fix "Working directory access". On a host with no working directory, fix "Data folder access". The fix closes the tree to Administrators, Hyper-V Administrators and SYSTEM. It also takes back what somebody else owns.
- The refusal names who and where. The fix does not remove a link in the tree, or correct a folder above the tree that somebody else can change. Do this yourself.
- The outcome of the fix names each item that it took back from another account. If you did not put an item there, examine it before you run a job.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-011` — The package changed after the job built it, so it was not signed

The job recorded the package's SHA-256 when it packed it. Before it signs, the application reads the package again and compares. The package was different, was gone, was a link or had a second name, or the job has no recorded hash. Somebody or something changed it in the job folder. It was not signed with your certificate.

**What to do:**

- Build the job again. You cannot sign a package that changed again: nothing tells what it contains now.
- Run host preparation and fix "Working directory access", so that only administrators can change the job folders.
- If you did not change the package, find who could write to the job folder before you build again.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-012` — AI agents do not sign on this host

An AI agent asked to sign a package again through MCP. This job was signed with your certificate, and on this host agents do not sign with your certificates. A package carries the identity of the certificate that signs it.

**What to do:**

- Retry signing on the Jobs screen.
- To let agents sign, go to Settings > AI agents (MCP). Select Ask each time or Allowed, then select the certificates.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-013` — Nobody confirmed that the agent's job can sign

On this host, the MCP client asks before an agent's job signs. The person declined or cancelled the question, or the client cannot ask questions. Nothing was signed.

**What to do:**

- Start the job again and accept the question in your MCP client.
- Use an MCP client that can ask questions, or build the job on the Build screen.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-SG-014` — The package is signed with a test certificate

An AI agent started this job, and on this host agents do not sign with your certificates. The package has your publisher, but a test certificate signed it. The product does not export it.

**What to do:**

- On the Jobs screen, select the job, then select Sign for release. The job is signed with your certificate and then exported.
- On the command line, run sign-for-release with the job ID.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-VF` — Verification

### `AP-VF-001` — The finished package would not install

The smoke test ran Add-AppxPackage on the package of this job, and Windows refused it. The package cannot be used. The job fails here, and not later at a customer.

**Observed:** Add-AppxPackage failed on a package that the conversion reported as successful.

**What to do:**

- 0x80073CF3 means that a declared framework dependency is not present. This is the false Windows App SDK dependency that the packaging tool adds. The product should have removed it, see AP-PK-006.
- 0x800B0109 means that this machine does not trust the signing certificate. A certificate from a CA needs no trust setup. A self-signed certificate needs it.
- 0x80073D02 means that a package with the same identity is already installed and running.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-VF-002` — The packaged application would not start

The package installed correctly, but the application did not start. The package deploys and does nothing. The smoke test exists to find this failure.

**What to do:**

- Make sure that the entry point in the manifest exists in the package files. A shortcut to a file that the installer did not install causes this.
- An application that needs a PSF fixup to find its own files often fails here first.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-VF-003` — The packaged application started and closed immediately

The application started and stopped before the settle time ended. It crashed at startup. Usually, it did not find something that it expected.

**What to do:**

- Check if the application writes to its own installation folder when it starts for the first time. That needs the FileRedirectionFixup. Without it, the application stops here.
- Look in the Application event log of the worker for the crash. The log names the missing assembly or file.

**Retry:** Possibly, but understand the cause first.

### `AP-VF-004` — The signing certificate is not trusted on the target

The package is built and signed correctly, but the machine that installs it does not trust the signing certificate. The package has no problem.

**Observed:** Add-AppxPackage failed with 0x800B0109 on a package that installs correctly on a machine that has the issuing certificate.

**What to do:**

- A certificate from a public CA needs no trust setup. This is the practical difference between a real certificate and a test certificate.
- For an internal CA, put the issuing certificate in Trusted Root or Trusted People on each target machine. Usually, Group Policy or Intune does this.
- For a self-signed certificate, each target needs that certificate. This does not scale. Use it only for development, not for deployment.
- Trust setup belongs to the deployment tool, not to this product. If a package installs only because the packaging host trusted something, it does not install anywhere else.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

## `AP-LC` — Licence

### `AP-LC-001` — The licence file is not valid

The signature check of the licence failed. The product does not run with a forged or damaged licence.

**What to do:**

- Download the licence file again. Usually, the file was damaged during transfer or changed by hand.
- If it still fails, contact support with the licence identifier.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-002` — The licence has expired and is in its grace period

Builds continue for 30 days after the licence expires, with a banner that stays. This is a warning, not a failure.

**What to do:**

- Renew the licence before the grace period ends.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-LC-003` — The licence has expired

The 30-day grace period is over, so the product refuses new builds. Job history, logs, output and the support information stay available. You keep access to your own data.

**What to do:**

- Renew the licence to build again.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-004` — The licence expires soon

This shows from 60 days before the licence expires. It is only a warning, and nothing is restricted yet.

**What to do:**

- Renew the licence.

**Retry:** Not applicable. This is informational rather than a failure.

### `AP-LC-005` — The system clock has moved backwards

The clock is much earlier than the latest date that the product recorded. The product accepts small changes back, for time zone changes, restored virtual machines and normal drift. It refuses a large change.

**What to do:**

- Set the system clock correctly.
- If the machine was restored from an old backup, set the clock correctly to fix this.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-006` — The starter allowance is used

Without a licence, this installation can build one image and five packages in its lifetime. A deleted image or package does not give its place back. The allowance is used, so the product refuses new builds. Job history, logs, output, and the images and packages already made stay available. You can still update and rebuild the image that you built.

**What to do:**

- Install a licence under Settings > Licence to build more.
- A community licence is free. Ask for one.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.

### `AP-LC-007` — The licence does not include MCP

The host service accepts an MCP client only with a licence that includes the mcp feature. The starter allowance and a community licence do not include it.

**What to do:**

- Install a Basic licence that includes MCP under Settings > Licence.
- Ask your supplier for a new licence file if your Basic licence does not include MCP.

**Retry:** No. Retrying reproduces the same failure.
